# Mesh/Model Editing Pipeline — `cart/editor`

## Important upfront note on disk layout

The task brief describes `mesh/doc.blob` + `mesh/parts.json` as the norm, but on disk there are **two coexisting package formats**:
- **Legacy / most packages** (`new_mesh_001`, `car`, `m4a1`, `pepes`): `manifest.json` + `mesh/base.blob` + `mesh/editmesh.json` (the studio authored-parts JSON).
- **Full meshdoc packages** (`Nude_Girl`): `manifest.json` + `mesh/base.blob` + `mesh/doc.blob` + `mesh/parts.json` + `atlases/base.png` + `paints/paint_N.{png,json}` + a source `.glb`.

Both are read; `editmesh.json` and `doc.blob`/`parts.json` are different generations of the same "parts" idea. Details in §2.

There is **no `characters/` dir yet** — only `props/`, `build/`, `roundtrip/` exist under `cart/editor/data/models/`. A player/NPC model would be the first `kind: 'character'` package.

---

## 1. File menu / New-Mesh flow

**Menu bar render:** `shell/Chrome.tsx:40-50` maps `MENUS` (`data/commands.ts:11`) into pressable items; clicking dispatches `props.onMenu(menu)`. The dropdown itself is `shell/DropdownMenu.tsx`, laid out from the tree in `data/commands.ts`.

**The command registry** is `data/commands.ts`. It is the source of truth. Relevant pieces:

- `PRIMITIVE_MESHES` (`commands.ts:17-25`) — the 7 starter primitives (cube/cylinder/cone/pyramid/plane/sphere/icosphere).
- `NEW_MESH_COMMANDS` (`commands.ts:28-31`) — auto-generated `new-mesh-<kind>` commands, `menu:'File', submenu:'New Mesh', scope:'global'`.
- `ADD_MESH_COMMANDS` (`commands.ts:34-37`) — `add-mesh-<kind>`, `menu:'Edit', submenu:'Add Primitive', scope:'model'`.
- Menu tree (`commands.ts:309-330`): `File` contains `{kind:'sub', id:'New Mesh', ... children: NEW_MESH_COMMANDS}` at line 312.

**Yes, "New Mesh" already exists** and is fully wired. There is also a `NewMeshDialog` (`shell/NewMeshDialog.tsx`) — a size/resolution prompt shown before the mesh is created.

**Dispatch path in `shell/AppFrame.tsx`:**

- `new-mesh-<kind>` clicked → `AppFrame.tsx:573-578` sets `state.newMeshPrompt = { kind, mode:'new' }`.
- `add-mesh-<kind>` clicked → `AppFrame.tsx:338-340` sets `newMeshPrompt = { kind, mode:'add' }`.
- Dialog renders at `AppFrame.tsx:2779-2785`; its `onAdd` → `submitMeshPrompt(prompt, params)` (`AppFrame.tsx:1503-1506`).
- `submitMeshPrompt` routes: `mode:'add'` → `addPrimitivePart`; `mode:'new'` → **`createNewMeshDocument`** (`AppFrame.tsx:1480-1500`).

**`createNewMeshDocument(kind, params)` — the "new model document" code path** (`AppFrame.tsx:1480-1500`):
```
const mid  = nextPrimitiveDocId(kind, prev.workspaceDocuments);   // 'primitive:cube:3'
const doc  = modelDocument(primitiveModelPackage(mid));           // a WorkspaceDocument
const base = makePart(kind, [], prev.seq, params);                // a ModelPart w/ EditMesh
const range = composeModelParts([base]).ranges[0];
const part: ModelPart = { ...base, lo, hi };
// -> workspaceDocuments: upsertDocument(...), activeWorkspaceDocumentId: doc.id,
//    modelParts: { [mid]: [part] }, modelActivePartId: part.id
```

This is **entirely in-memory state** — no disk write. The doc opens in the editor immediately; persistence only happens on Save (§5). Supporting factories:
- `primitiveModelPackage(id)` — `data/content.ts:175-198`.
- `nextPrimitiveDocId(kind, docs)` — `data/content.ts:236-243`.
- `modelDocument(pkg)` — `data/documents.ts:12`.
- `makePart(kind, existing, seq, params)` — `AppFrame.tsx:1424-1428` (calls `primitivePartMesh`).

There is also an env hook `RJIT_MODELDOC=<kind>` at `AppFrame.tsx:1511-1514` that boots straight into a fresh doc — useful for headless repro of a "new model" path.

---

## 2. Model packages on disk

**Directory layout & manifest** are owned by `data/modelPackage.ts`:
- `MODELS_HOME = 'cart/editor/data/models'` (`:30`); subdirs `['mesh','atlases','paints','shaders']` (`:35`).
- `categoryDir(kind)` (`:73`): prop→`props`, character→`characters`, vehicle→`vehicles`, build→`build`.
- `packageDirForName(kind, name)` (`:94`) — the preferred home is named after the model NAME, slugified.

**`ModelManifest` schema** (`data/modelPackage.ts:41-69`):
```ts
type ModelManifest = {
  version: number; id: string; name: string;
  kind: 'build'|'prop'|'character'|'vehicle';
  stage: 'wip'|'ready'|'locked';
  favorite?: boolean; hidden?: boolean;
  folderId: ContentFolderId; semanticKind?: string; sourceKind?: ...;
  color: string; rig: string; data: string;
  triangles: number; lods: number;
  mesh: { viewerPath?: string; viewerMeshRef?: string };
  decompositions: string[]; atlases: ModelAtlas[]; paints: ModelPaintVariant[];
  placeable?: ModelPlaceable;   // req_2718 — disk is the placeability truth
  skeleton?: Skeleton;          // req_2712 — exported rig
};
```
`packageToManifest` / `manifestToPackage` convert to/from the in-memory `ModelPackage` (`data/types.ts:316-349`). Written by `materializeModelPackage` (`data/modelPackageStore.ts:138-152`) — manifest is written **last** as the commit point.

**`mesh/base.blob`** — raw interleaved verts, **stride 8 f32 per vert** (pos3 / normal3 / uv2), little-endian, no header. Emitted by host door `__model_mesh_write` (`modelPackageStore.ts:158, 427`). It's the meshdoc reader's legacy fallback (one part, identity face groups).

**`mesh/doc.blob`** — **RJMD v1** format, defined and parsed in `data/meshDoc.ts`. Header is 6× u32 = 24 bytes: `[magic=0x444d4a52 'RJMD', version=1, vertCount, faceCount, hasGroups, rangeCount]`, then `vertCount*8` f32 verts, then optional `faceCount` u32 face-group ids, then `rangeCount` `[lo,hi)` u32 pairs. Written by host door `__model_meshdoc_write` (`meshDoc.ts:57`). The TS type:
```ts
// data/meshDoc.ts:27-34
type PackageMeshDoc = {
  vertices: Float32Array;            // stride 8 pos3/normal3/uv2
  faceGroups: Uint32Array | null;    // one authored-group id per triangle
  ranges: { lo: number; hi: number }[];  // per-part [lo,hi) authored-group ranges
};
```

**`mesh/parts.json`** — rank-ordered part METADATA matching `doc.blob`'s ranges (`meshDoc.ts:37`):
```ts
type MeshDocPartMeta = { name: string; color: string; visible: boolean; kind?: string };
// file: { "version": 1, "parts": [ {name,color,visible,kind?}, ... ] }
```
`readMeshDoc`/`readMeshDocParts`/`writeMeshDoc` (`meshDoc.ts:56-89`), cached per dir, invalidated by its own writers.

**`mesh/editmesh.json`** — the older studio parts format (raw authored `EditMesh` per part): `{ "version":1, "parts":[ { id, name, mesh:{ verts:[[x,y,z]...], faces/quads... }, color, visible } ] }`. Written via `materializeSnapshotPackage`'s `editMeshJson` blob (`modelPackageStore.ts:162, 190`). Loaded into `storedModelPartsById` (see below).

**`atlases/base.png`** — model texture atlas, written by `__image_write_png` in `writeModelArtifacts` (`modelPackageStore.ts:430-433`). **`paints/paint_N.{png,json}`** — paint variants, handled by `data/paintVariants.ts` + `library/ModelPaintVariants.tsx`.

**Catalog / library loading** (`library/` + `data/`):
- `loadMaterializedPackages()` / `hasMaterializedPackages()` (`modelPackageStore.ts:360-397`) scan disk → `manifestToPackage`.
- `storedModelParts(modelId)` (`hmscAssetCatalog.ts:247-273`) returns parsed studio parts (`buildStoredModelParts` → `storedPartToModelPart`).
- Package→mesh resolution: `modelPackageMeshData` (`hmscAssetCatalog.ts:206`), `packageMeshDoc`/`packageMeshDocParts` (`:234-239`).
- UI: `library/LibraryPanel.tsx`, `ModelPackageBrowser.tsx`, `ModelDetailBody.tsx`, `ModelThumbnail.tsx` + `modelThumb.ts`; content tree in `data/content.ts` (folders like `models-characters` at `content.ts:69,140`; category node table at `hmscAssetCatalog.ts:1045-1068`).

## 3. The mesh editor itself

**Where it lives:**
- **`model/editMesh.ts`** (137 KB) — the pure, headless mesh document model + all generators + topology ops. CLONED from `cart/hmsc-int` (see header `editMesh.ts:1-14`).
- **`stage/ModelView.tsx`** (138 KB) — the host-native 3D editor surface that owns live tool dispatch, the host mesh, gizmos, painting, journal calls.
- **`stage/ModelOutliner.tsx`** — the PART list outliner.
- **`stage/ModelDocumentSurface.tsx`**, `stage/ModelContextMenu.tsx`, `stage/ToolOptions.tsx` — surrounding UI.
- **`inspector/RigSection.tsx`** — the rig panel (§5).

**The mesh document model** (`model/editMesh.ts`):
```ts
// editMesh.ts:108-131
type EditMesh = {
  verts: V3[];                 // V3 = [number,number,number]
  faces: EditMeshFace[];
  mounts?: MountPoint[];       // typed connection points (Lego stud/anti-stud)
  pivot?: V3;                  // part-local rotation origin (sticky once set)
  slots?: TextureSlot[];       // named re-skinnable face groups
  lights?: LightRig[];         // per-part authored lights
};
// editMesh.ts:23-40
type EditMeshFace = {
  loop: number[];              // CCW vertex-index loop, 3+ corners — QUAD-FRIENDLY n-gon
  uv?: V2[];                   // per-corner UV, stable (assigned once by unwrap())
  material?: number;           // atlas/slot index
  glass?: boolean;             // translucent pane
  tag?: number;                // transient provenance tag
};
```
Geometry is stored as **shared verts + n-gon faces (quad-friendly loops)**, NOT triangle soup or fixed quads. It **lowers** to triangle `GeometryData` via `editMeshToGeometry(m, includeFace?, faceGroupsOut?)` (`editMesh.ts:608`), which also emits one authored-face-group id per triangle.

**Generators** (each returns an `EditMesh`): `cuboid` (`:659`), `cylinder` (`:690`), `cone` (`:723`), `pyramid` (`:747`), `plane` (`:765`), `sphere` (`:788`), `icosphere` (`:827`), plus `latticePanel` (`:895`), `wheelMesh` (`:1320`). Editing ops: `mergeMesh` (`:1334`), `translateVerts`/`rotateVerts`/`scaleVerts` (`:1350-1398`), `cutMeshByPlane` (`:1398`), `loopCut` (`:1479`), `splitQuad`/`splitConcaveFaces` (`:1025-1063`), `mirrorMesh`/`symmetrize` (`:203/439`), `unwrap`/`unwrapMesh` (`:1094/1212`), plus mounts/pivots/lights helpers.

**How parts appear** — `ModelPart` (`data/types.ts:28-52`):
```ts
type ModelPart = {
  id: string; name: string;
  kind?: PrimitiveKind;        // seed primitive, for naming/icons
  mesh?: EditMesh;             // seed geometry (initial compose only)
  sourcePath?: string;         // file-backed part (.glb/.obj parsed by host)
  visible: boolean; color: string; lift?: number;
  lo?: number; hi?: number;    // authored-group range in the composed host mesh
};
```
`state.modelParts: Record<string, ModelPart[]>` (`types.ts:503`) maps modelId → parts. Outliner renders these rows in `stage/ModelOutliner.tsx:34-83` (visibility eye, color chip, name, verb columns; multi-select set logic in `AppFrame.tsx:1515-1540`).

**Compose:** `composeModelParts(parts)` (`hmscAssetCatalog.ts:389-412`) concatenates each visible part's lowered geometry into ONE host mesh, assigning each part a contiguous face-group range `{id, lo, hi}`. This is how the outliner selects/highlights a whole part by range.

**Journal / ops:** the mesh journal is HOST-side, reached through doors — `__mesh_history` (`commands.ts:233`), `__mesh_paint_history` for paint strokes (`:225`). `undoDepths(state)` (`commands.ts:217-242`) reads the live depths; `ModelToolApi` (`types.ts:132`) is the cart→host command surface (e.g. `appendPart(positions, faceGroups, color)` used at `AppFrame.tsx:1468`). Undo/redo route per-surface in `runCommand` (model → host mesh journal, world → local stacks).

---

## 4. Creating a new model programmatically

**The existing "new model" path** is `createNewMeshDocument` (§1, `AppFrame.tsx:1480-1500`) — memory only. **Import** paths:
- `import-model-file` command (`commands.ts:84`) → host door `__mesh_load_file`.
- `fileModelPackage(source)` (`hmscAssetCatalog.ts:701`) and `importModelFilePackage(sourcePath)` (`:737`) — synthesize a `ModelPackage` from a `.glb/.obj` (a single `sourcePath`-backed part, `filePartSeed` at `AppFrame.tsx:1431`).
- `primitivePartMesh(kind, params)` (`hmscAssetCatalog.ts:379-381`) — build one part's `EditMesh`.

**Minimal set of writes to create a package that opens in the editor:**

To open in the *current session* (no disk): construct a `ModelPackage`, wrap with `modelDocument`, seed `state.modelParts[id] = ModelPart[]` (each with an `EditMesh` or `sourcePath`), set `activeWorkspaceDocumentId`. That's exactly what `createNewMeshDocument` does.

To *persist* it (so it reopens & appears in the library):
1. `materializeModelPackage(pkg)` (`modelPackageStore.ts:138`) → writes the package dir + subdirs + **manifest.json**. For a model with pre-authored parts (no resident host mesh), use `materializeSnapshotPackage(pkg, blobs)` (`:174-197`) to drop `mesh/base.blob` / `mesh/editmesh.json` / `atlases/base.png` alongside.
2. `writeModelArtifacts(pkg, parts?)` (`modelPackageStore.ts:421-436`) → `__model_mesh_write` → `mesh/base.blob`; `writeMeshDoc(dir, parts)` → `mesh/doc.blob` (via `__model_meshdoc_write`) + `mesh/parts.json`; atlas PNG if resident. **This is what makes a package REOPEN as the edited document.**
3. `registerSavedPackage(pkg)` (`content.ts:248`) so this session's library sees it.

For a **multi-part player model** authored purely in JS (no host mesh yet), the cleanest route is `materializeSnapshotPackage` with an `editMeshJson` blob of the parts (mirrors how studio models persist), OR seed `state.modelParts` and let the host mesh + `writeModelArtifacts` capture it on Save.

---

## 5. Export

Handlers live in `runCommand` in `shell/AppFrame.tsx`:
- **`save-snapshot`** (`AppFrame.tsx:449-494`) — "Save Model to Library": `materializeModelPackage` (manifest) + `writeModelArtifacts` (base.blob + doc.blob + parts.json + atlas). A live rig draft is compiled onto the package via `propRigToSkeleton` (`:470-472`).
- **`export-build-piece-<kind>` / `export-prop`** (`AppFrame.tsx:496-568`) — export the open model as a placeable. **The manifest is the placeability record (req_2718):** it writes `placeable` (`ModelPlaceable`, `types.ts:314`) + the compiled `skeleton` into the package via `updateManifestPlaceable` (`modelPackageStore.ts:250`) or a first `materializeModelPackage`. Export implies save — `writeModelArtifacts` runs first (`:520`) so the geometry you SEE is captured. Bounds are measured off the real mesh (`authoredMeshBounds`) and the prop rig is compiled with `propRigToSkeleton(modelId, modelId, rig, bounds)` (`:536`).

**Hash-named binary asset:** content-addressed mesh blobs are the "cooked asset" path — `viewerMeshRef`, `cookedMeshRefForAsset(assetId)` (`hmscAssetCatalog.ts:191`), `cookedMeshBlobData(ref)` (`:186`); manifest `data: "hash <short>"` (`:951`). A saved/exported model resolves its mesh through `viewerMeshRef` when present (`:215, 525`). The FNV hash helper is at `hmscAssetCatalog.ts:1289-1292`.

**Rigging vocabulary — `runtime/skeleton/`** (NOT in the cart; imported by the editor):
- **`runtime/skeleton/rigs.ts`** — the canonical rig vocabulary + templates. Key exports:
  - `PropRig` (`rigs.ts:94-103`): `{ container?, placements?, seat?, cover?, dynamics? }`; `ItemRig` (`:208-213`).
  - `propRigToSkeleton(id, geometryKey, rig, bounds)` (`:126`) / `skeletonToPropRig` (`:166`) / `describePropRig` (`:192`).
  - Contact/mount name vocab: `POCKET_PREFIX`, `PLACEMENT_PREFIX`, `SEAT_PREFIX`, `GRIP_LEFT/RIGHT`, `AMMO_MOUNT`, `PROJECTILE_MOUNT` (`:23-40`).
  - **Formation templates — directly relevant to Player/NPC:** `bodyRigBones()` (`rigs.ts:248-277`) — the full humanoid formation (body→abdomen→chest→head, mirrored `shoulder/upper_arm/elbow/lower_arm/wrist/hand/fingers` and `hip/upper_leg/knee/lower_leg/foot/toes`), and `carRigBones()` (`:281-304`). **These are currently only used in `rigs.test.ts` — NOT wired into any editor UI yet.**
- **`runtime/skeleton/schema.ts`** — the `Skeleton` object model: `Bone` (`:51`), `Joint` (`kind: fixed|hinge|slide|pivot|spin`, `:38-46`), `Meshes` (`perBone` | `skinned`, `:81-83`), `Contact`/`Mount`/`NamedBehavior`, `Skeleton` (`:126-138`), and builders `defineSkeleton` (`:145`) / `staticProp` (`:154`).
- `inspector/RigSection.tsx` — the rig panel; **prop-only today** (`PropRig` container/placements/seat/cover/dynamics, `:26-135`). No body/character rig UI exists.

## 6. Player in `cart/editor/PlayRoute.tsx`

`PlayRoute.tsx` (whole file, 24 lines) mounts the host-native world loader on the compiled game file:
```jsx
createElement('WorldLoader', {
  gameFile: 'zig-out/game/hmsc.gamefile',
  storeDir: 'zig-out/game/contentstore',
  ...
})
```
`WorldLoader` is a host primitive (framework `world_loader.zig` / `v8_bindings_compiled_world.zig`). **The cart contains no player geometry** — the player model is whatever the compiled gamefile/contentstore carries, rendered entirely host-side. Searching the cart for `player`/`npc`/`character` finds only the `character` package *kind* and content-tree folders (`content.ts`, `types.ts`, `hmscAssetCatalog.ts`), not any player mesh. So /play does not render a cart-authored player today.

---

## Where to hook in "New Mesh → Player/NPC model"

Concretely, the seams:

1. **Command + menu** — add a submenu or leaf under `File → New Mesh` in `data/commands.ts` (alongside `NEW_MESH_COMMANDS`, `:28-31`, and the tree at `:312`). E.g. `new-model-player` / `new-model-npc`, `scope:'global'`.

2. **Dispatch** — in `AppFrame.tsx` (mirror the `new-mesh-` branch at `:573-578`), add a handler that builds a multi-part character model. Follow `createNewMeshDocument` (`:1480-1500`) but:
   - Build a `ModelPackage` of `kind:'character'` (new factory alongside `primitiveModelPackage`, `content.ts:175`; category dir `characters` already handled at `modelPackage.ts:76`).
   - Seed `state.modelParts[id]` with a `ModelPart[]` — one part per body region. You need to author each part's `EditMesh` (use the generators in `editMesh.ts`, e.g. `cuboid`/`cylinder`/`sphere`, positioned with `lift`/`translateVerts`). Give each part a name matching a bone from `bodyRigBones()` so the outliner reads as the skeleton.
   - Optionally attach `skeleton: defineSkeleton(id, bodyRigBones(), { meshes:{kind:'perBone',...} })` (`schema.ts:145`, `rigs.ts:248`).

3. **New generator** — add a `genPlayerModel()` / `genNpcModel()` producing the `ModelPart[]` (probably a new file in `model/` or `data/`, reusing `editMesh.ts` generators + `bodyRigBones()` naming). This is the main **data to generate**: a list of `{name, mesh: EditMesh, color, visible}` parts.

4. **Persistence** — `materializeModelPackage` + `writeModelArtifacts` (or `materializeSnapshotPackage` with `editMeshJson`) already handle writing the package; the manifest `kind:'character'` + a `bodyRigBones()` skeleton is the "truth" per req_2718. The `characters/` dir will be created on first save.

5. **Rig UI (optional later)** — `inspector/RigSection.tsx` is prop-only; a character/body rig editor would be a new section driven by `bodyRigBones()` — currently unused, so that's greenfield.</result>
